# Factions & Organizations

## Aid Society {#aid-society}

The Aid Society is a local group whose members, including women like Mrs. Jasper Bell, periodically gather at members' homes such as [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables) for meetings and tea.

**Members:** [Lynde](../character/lynde.md), [Marilla Cuthbert](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md), [Rachel Lynde](../character/rachel-lynde.md)

> [Marilla](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md) returns to [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables) with the orphaned twins, [Davy](../character/davy-keith.md) and [Dora](../character/dora.md), whose playful and rowdy behavior immediately poses a challenge for [Marilla](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md) and [Anne](../character/anne.md). At church on Sunday, [Davy](../character/davy-keith.md) creates a commotion by dropping a caterpillar down [Lauretta](../character/lauretta.md) White's neck during the service. Later in the week, [Davy](../character/davy-keith.md) ruins Dora's dress by forcing her to walk the pigpen fence and pumps water over her, subsequently confessing to [Anne](../character/anne.md) that he also hid a toad in Marilla's bed.
>
> — v2 · VIII Marilla Adopts Twins

## Allans {#allans}

The Allans are guests and loved acquaintances of [Anne](../character/anne.md) who, along with Miss [Stacy](../character/stacy.md), were invited to dinner at [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables).

## American {#american}

The Americans are wealthy summer visitors, including artists and millionaires, who frequent local hotels like the [White Sands Hotel](../codex/places.md#white-sands-hotel) for the coastal scenery.

## Bluenose {#bluenose}

A Bluenose is a term associated with native inhabitants and old, exclusive families of [Nova Scotia](../codex/places.md#nova-scotia), such as those hailing from [Bolingbroke](../codex/places.md#bolingbroke).

## Blythes {#blythes}

The Blythes are a local family whose children, including [Di](../character/di.md), are close friends with the Meredith youngsters from the manse, frequently spending time together in [Rainbow Valley](../codex/places.md#rainbow-valley).

## Boulters {#boulters}

The Boulters are a local family, including Levi, Milty, and Mrs. Boulter, who are noted by others for their business savvy, stinginess, and contrary nature.

## Canadian Woman {#canadian-woman}

The Canadian Woman is a publication that prints short stories and other literary works by contributors like Margaret Burton.

## Christians {#christians}

Christians are people who attend church and are interred in designated church graveyards.

## Conduct Club {#conduct-club}

Suggested by [Jem Blythe](../character/jem.md), the Good-Conduct Club is a secret self-governing organization formed by the Meredith children to improve their behavior and avoid disgrace by self-enforcing rules and self-inflicted punishments.

**Members:** [Carl](../character/carl.md), [Faith](../character/faith.md), [Jerry](../character/jerry.md), [Una Meredith](../character/una-meredith.md)

> [Faith](../character/faith.md) causes a scandal at church by attending without stockings, which leads to gossip across the [Glen](../codex/places.md#glen) and discussions among [Anne](../character/anne.md), [Susan](../character/susan.md), and Miss Cornelia. In [Rainbow Valley](../codex/places.md#rainbow-valley), [Nan](../character/nan-blythe.md) and [Di](../character/di.md) defend [Faith](../character/faith.md) when [Mary Vance](../character/mary-vance.md) criticizes her, but [Jerry](../character/jerry.md) and the Conduct Club decide to punish [Faith](../character/faith.md) by making her wear her hated striped stockings. To clear her father's name and clarify other misunderstandings, [Faith](../character/faith.md) writes and publishes a detailed letter of explanation in the local newspaper.
>
> — v5 · CHAPTER XXV. ANOTHER SCANDAL AND ANOTHER “EXPLANATION”

## Conservative {#conservative}

The Conservatives, also known as Tories, are a Canadian political party that held power for eighteen years prior to being defeated in a general election by the Liberals.

**Members:** [Anne](../character/anne.md), [Cornelia Bryant](../character/cornelia-bryant.md), [Gilbert Blythe](../character/gilbert-blythe.md), [Gus](../character/gus.md), [Marilla Cuthbert](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md), [Matthew](../character/matthew.md)

## Cottons {#cottons}

The Cottons are a family consisting of a mother, older sisters, and four younger, wild, and sunburned children named Pete, [Tommy](../character/tommy.md), Adolphus, and [Mirabel](../character/mirabel-cotton.md) who live near a woods and brook.

**Members:** [Tommy](../character/tommy.md)

## Crawfords {#crawfords}

The Crawfords are a family residing on the far side of [Four Winds Harbor](../codex/places.md#four-winds-harbor) who are locally noted for their vainglory, cleverness, and passionate, lifelong involvement in politics.

## Cuthberts {#cuthberts}

The Cuthberts are a quiet and reserved family residing at [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables), a secluded and meticulously clean homestead situated at the edge of cleared land in [Avonlea](../codex/places.md#avonlea).

## Debating Club {#debating-club}

[The Avonlea](../codex/places.md#avonlea) Debating Club is a respectable local organization that meets fortnightly throughout the winter and hosts entertainments at the hall, such as a major paid concert featuring music, recitations, and an address by the minister to benefit the library.

## Douglases {#douglases}

The Douglases are a close-knit, generous clan whose financial support accounts for half of Mr. Meredith's salary at the church.

## Eaton {#eaton}

_Not yet known._

## Elliotts {#elliotts}

The Elliotts are a family residing on the other side of [Four Winds](../codex/places.md#four-winds) harbor who are renowned for their conceit, stubbornness, cleverness, and dyed-in-the-wool political convictions.

## Episcopalians {#episcopalians}

The Episcopalians are a religious denomination whose members include the [West](../character/west.md) family and who have a church located at [Lowbridge](../codex/places.md#lowbridge).

**Members:** [Ellen West](../character/ellen-west.md), [Rosemary West](../character/rosemary-west.md)

## German {#german}

Germans are a nation associated with a strong sense of militarism under their Kaiser as well as a complex system of theology.

## Grit {#grit}

The Grits, also known as the Liberals, are a Canadian political party that succeeded in securing a sweeping majority in a general election after eighteen years of [Tory](../codex/factions.md#conservative) rule.

**Members:** [Gilbert Blythe](../character/gilbert-blythe.md), [Marshall](../character/marshall.md), [Uncle Jim](../character/uncle-jim.md)

## Improvement Society {#improvement-society}

The Improvement Society is an [Avonlea](../codex/places.md#avonlea) organization conceived by [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md) and supported by local youth to make the village prettier through projects like cleaning up land, removing dilapidated structures, and repainting the hall.

**Members:** [Anne](../character/anne.md), [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md), [Di](../character/di.md), [Diana](../character/diana.md), [Fred Wright](../character/fred-wright.md), [Gertie Pye](../character/gertie-pye.md), [Gilbert Blythe](../character/gilbert-blythe.md), [Jane](../character/jane.md), [Jane Andrews](../character/jane-andrews.md), [Julia Bell](../character/julia-bell.md), [Oliver Sloane](../character/oliver-sloane.md)

> [Anne](../character/anne.md) nervously visits Mr. [Harrison](../character/harrison.md) to confess that she accidentally sold his Jersey cow to Mr. [Shearer](../character/shearer.md). To her relief, Mr. [Harrison](../character/harrison.md) takes the mistake good-naturedly, accepts Anne's cow in exchange, and invites her to stay for tea. After sharing a pleasant conversation and bonding over cake and tea, [Anne](../character/anne.md) returns home to happily report the successful outcome to [Marilla](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md).
>
> — v2 · III Mr. Harrison at Home

## Improvers {#improvers}

The Improvers, also known as the [Avonlea](../codex/places.md#avonlea) Village [Improvement Society](../codex/factions.md#improvement-society) (A.V.I.S.), is a flourishing local organization that works to beautify the community through projects such as clearing road fronts, planting flower beds, and petitioning for improvements to public and church grounds.

**Members:** [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md), [Diana](../character/diana.md), [Fred Wright](../character/fred-wright.md), [Gertie Pye](../character/gertie-pye.md), [Jane](../character/jane.md), [Julia Bell](../character/julia-bell.md), [Priscilla Grant](../character/priscilla-grant.md)

> [Anne](../character/anne.md) walks home with Mrs. [Lynde](../character/lynde.md), who talks about church preparations, and upon returning home, [Anne](../character/anne.md) and [Marilla](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md) learn from a letter that the twins will stay with them until fall. [Anne](../character/anne.md) recalls a humorous interaction with [Davy](../character/davy-keith.md) regarding his antics and misinterpretations of the catechism. Later, at an Improvers meeting, the group is distressed to hear that [Judson Parker](../character/judson-parker.md) plans to rent his fence for advertisements, and an unsuccessful committee sent to reason with him leaves them dismayed.
>
> — v2 · XIV A Danger Averted

> [Anne](../character/anne.md), [Diana](../character/diana.md), and Jane plead with [Judson Parker](../character/judson-parker.md) not to rent his fences for patent medicine ads, but he refuses. Later, [Anne](../character/anne.md) accidentally overhears Judson taking a political bribe from [Jerry Corcoran](../character/jerry.md) near the Lake of [Shining Waters](../codex/places.md#shining-waters). Fearing [Anne](../character/anne.md) will expose his corruption and ruin his reputation, Judson agrees to cancel the ad deal to keep her quiet, though [Anne](../character/anne.md) refuses to make a deal and simply keeps the secret out of principle.
>
> — v2 · XIV A Danger Averted

> [Anne](../character/anne.md) completes her school year and walks home, meeting young [Paul Irving](../character/paul-irving.md) on her way to the [Avonlea](../codex/places.md#avonlea) cemetery. They discuss their loved ones, imagination, and placing flowers on graves. At the cemetery, [Anne](../character/anne.md) meets Mrs. [Allan](../character/allan.md), and the two walk home together while discussing teaching, ideals, friendship, and future plans.
>
> — v2 · XV The Beginning of Vacation

## Indian {#indian}

The Indians are a cultural group whose traditional headdresses, made of colorful feathers, are imitated by local schoolboys.

## Liberal {#liberal}

The Liberal party is a political group whose members include [Rachel Lynde](../character/rachel-lynde.md), old [Martin](../character/martin.md) Bovyer, and [Diana](../character/diana.md) Barry's father.

**Members:** [Diana](../character/diana.md), [Rachel Lynde](../character/rachel-lynde.md)

## MacAllisters {#macallisters}

The MacAllisters are a prominent, thick population of brainy, prideful, and fiercely partisan people who heavily settle the far side of the [Four Winds](../codex/places.md#four-winds) harbor.

## Merediths {#merediths}

The Merediths are the children of the local widower minister, known for their unrestrained freedom and inclination to offend others, including local [Methodists](../codex/factions.md#methodist), through their unguided antics.

## Methodist {#methodist}

The Methodists are a local religious group whose members maintain their own minister, church, prayer-meetings, and graveyard, and whose potential unification with the [Presbyterians](../codex/factions.md#presbyterian) is a subject of local debate.

**Members:** [Baxter](../character/baxter.md), [Fiske](../character/fiske.md), [Howard](../character/howard.md)

## Presbyterian {#presbyterian}

The Presbyterians are a Christian religious denomination that maintains its own church and choir, whose staunch adherents, such as Miss Cornelia, strongly prefer its practice and faith over those of the local [Methodists](../codex/factions.md#methodist).

**Members:** [Anne](../character/anne.md), [Cooper](../character/cooper.md), [Cornelia Bryant](../character/cornelia-bryant.md), [Elder Clow](../character/elder-clow.md), [Leavitt](../character/leavitt.md), [Leslie Moore](../character/leslie-moore.md), [Uncle Jim](../character/uncle-jim.md)

> Miss Cornelia asks about Anne's encounter with [Leslie Moore](../character/leslie-moore.md) on the shore and encourages [Anne](../character/anne.md) to persist in being Leslie's friend despite her cold demeanor. [Anne](../character/anne.md) promises to do all she can to reach out to the lonely, tragic [Leslie](../character/leslie-moore.md), and Miss Cornelia reassures [Anne](../character/anne.md) of Leslie's true Presbyterian faith.
>
> — v4 · CHAPTER 11 THE STORY OF LESLIE MOORE

## Pyes {#pyes}

The Pyes are a localized group of four interconnected families known for being domineering, unsociable, and stubborn, whose members include Roger, Joshua, [John Andrew](../character/john-andrew.md), and Anthony.

## Rollings Reliable {#rollings-reliable}

Rollings Reliable is a [Montreal](../codex/places.md#montreal)-based baking powder company that hosted a story competition to advertise its product, offering a twenty-five dollar prize for the winning entry.

## Sloanes {#sloanes}

The Sloanes are a village family regarded as good, honest, and respectable people, though defined by an inherently distinct and unchanging family nature.

**Members:** [Charlie Sloane](../character/charlie-sloane.md)

## Story Club {#story-club}

The Story Club was an informal group formed during their schooldays by [Anne](../character/anne.md), [Diana](../character/diana.md), [Jane Andrews](../character/jane-andrews.md), and [Ruby Gillis](../character/ruby-gillis.md), where they wrote thrilling tales featuring dramatic plotlines and aristocratic names.

**Members:** [Anne](../character/anne.md), [Jane](../character/jane.md), [Jane Andrews](../character/jane-andrews.md)

## The Blythe {#the-blythe}

The [Blythes](../codex/factions.md#blythes) are a local family whose children—including [Jem](../character/jem.md), [Nan](../character/nan-blythe.md), and [Di](../character/di.md)—reside at [Ingleside](../codex/places.md#ingleside) and are well regarded by the manse children.

## The Meredith {#the-meredith}

The [Merediths](../codex/factions.md#merediths) are the lively, close-knit family of the Rev. John Knox Meredith, comprising his motherless children—[Jerry](../character/jerry.md), [Faith](../character/faith.md), [Una](../character/una-meredith.md), and [Carl](../character/carl.md)—and [Aunt Martha](../character/aunt-martha.md), who together reside at the [Glen](../codex/places.md#glen) St. Mary manse.

## Tree Lovers {#tree-lovers}

The Tree Lovers is the name given by [Walter](../character/walter.md) to a spruce tree and a maple tree growing so closely together in [Rainbow Valley](../codex/places.md#rainbow-valley) that their branches are inextricably intertwined.

## Wrights {#wrights}

The Wrights are a local family whose households include [Elisha Wright](../character/elisha-wright.md) in [Avonlea](../codex/places.md#avonlea)—who took in his wife's aunt Atossa—and the late Mrs. Isaac Wright of [White Sands](../codex/places.md#white-sands-hotel).

## Yankee {#yankee}

A term used to refer to [Americans](../codex/factions.md#american), the group is viewed with suspicion and prejudice by Mrs. Rachel [Lynde](../character/lynde.md), who holds the whole United [States](../codex/places.md#states) responsible for her husband once being cheated out of ten dollars in [Boston](../codex/places.md#boston).
